title: Open–closed reduction for the direct-image assertion
statement:
For a separated finite-type morphism $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ of separated
finite-type $k_0$-schemes, say that $f_0$ satisfies the
*direct-image assertion* if, for every $w\in\mathbf R$ and every
constructible Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X_0$ which is $\iota$-mixed of
weights at most $w$ ([def-weil-punctual-weights]), the sheaf
$R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w+r$ for
every $r$; say that $f_0$ satisfies the *complex form* of the assertion
if $Rf_{0!}$ carries $D_{\le w}(X_0)$ into $D_{\le w}(Y_0)$ for every
$w$ ([def-weil-complex-weights]).

1. *(Source.)* Let $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ be open with closed
   complement $i_0:Z_0\hookrightarrow X_0$. If the direct-image
   assertion (resp. its complex form) holds for $f_0j_0$ and $f_0i_0$,
   it holds for $f_0$.
1. *(Target.)* Let $j'_0:V_0\hookrightarrow Y_0$ be open with closed
   complement $i'_0:T_0\hookrightarrow Y_0$, and let
   $f_{V}:f_0^{-1}(V_0)\to V_0$, $f_T:f_0^{-1}(T_0)\to T_0$ be the
   restrictions of $f_0$. If the direct-image assertion (resp. its
   complex form) holds for $f_V$ and $f_T$, it holds for $f_0$.
   By induction, the same holds for any finite stratification of $Y_0$
   by locally closed pieces built from successive open–closed
   decompositions.
1. *(Coefficients.)* Fix $f_0$ and $w$, and let
   $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$ be an exact
   sequence of constructible Weil sheaves on $X_0$. If
   $R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F'$ and $R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F''$ are $\iota$-mixed
   of weights at most $w+r$ for every $r$, so is $R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F$.
   By induction on the length, the same holds for a finite filtration of
   $\mathcal F$ by Weil subsheaves.

proof.text: For source localization, take $\Lambda=\Qlb$ in [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages]. The immersions descend to $k_0$, so its arrows are equivariant. Clause (3) of [prop-functor-package] and [prop-weil-operations] give the underlying triangle with outer terms $R(f_0j_0)_!j_0^*K$ and $R(f_0i_0)_!i_0^*K$. These are bounded constructible: the schemes and maps are separated of finite type, $\ell\ne p$, and this is the field domain, with no smooth-base-change hypotheses.

By [lem-zl-immersion-pullback-weight-preservation], both source restrictions preserve the input bound. For $K\in D_{\le w}$ the source hypotheses bound the outer terms in step 1; [lem-zl-complex-extension] bounds the middle. For $K=F[0]$, [lem-zl-source-decomposition-cohomology] gives the exact degree-$r$ Weil segment; the sheaf hypotheses bound its endpoints by $w+r$, and [lem-zl-exact-middle-weight-bound] bounds the middle.

proof.text: For the target squares, the source maps are immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft]. The restrictions $f_V,f_T$ are separated of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. Apply immersion weight preservation to the input. Clause (4) of [prop-functor-package] and [prop-weil-operations] identify the restrictions of $M=Rf_{0!}K$ with the two restricted direct images, bounded by $w$. For $G=R^rf_{0!}F$, [lem-zl-immersion-higher-shriek-base-change] identifies its restrictions, bounded by $w+r$. Here arbitrary compact-support base change uses $D^b_c(-,\Qlb)$.

proof.text: The exact pure-preserving extension of [lem-zl-extension-by-zero-punctual] has the mixed and derived bound [lem-zl-open-shriek-weight-preservation]. The closed immersion is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]; [lem-zl-finite-pushforward] supplies the other preservation hypothesis of [lem-zl-target-weight-reassembly]. Apply reassembly to $M$ at $u=w$, or to $G[0]$ at $u=w+r$, proving both target assertions.

For coefficients, [lem-zl-weil-shriek-coefficient-long-exact] gives the exact segment $R^rf_{0!}F'\to R^rf_{0!}F\to R^rf_{0!}F''$. Apply [lem-zl-exact-middle-weight-bound] at $u=w+r$. Induct through $0\to F_{a-1}\to F_a\to F_a/F_{a-1}\to0$, starting at zero.
